clue.text: Average former England goalie escorting international socialite

indicators.note: one who escorts goes alongside a companion, so the goalie sits right beside the international in the line

parts.note: par is the average or normal standard
I is the abbreviation for international
Peter Shilton, England's most capped goalkeeper

explanation.surface: A middling ex-England keeper is seen out on the arm of a jet-setting international celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Shilton kept goal for England 125 times in the 1970s and 80s; the S of his name does double work, closing PARIS before HILTON begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The hotel heiress is famous chiefly as a celebrity party-goer, the archetypal modern socialite.

clue.text: Rodent seen when Frankie's chums go cycling

indicators.note: going round a cycle moves the front of the phrase to the back, rotating its order

parts.note: the Rat Pack were Frank Sinatra's circle of entertainer friends

explanation.surface: Sinatra's pals set off on a bike ride and a rat is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotate RAT PACK so its first word moves to the end. The Rat Pack were Sinatra, Dean Martin, Sammy Davis Jr and friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack rat is a North American woodrat, a rodent known for hoarding objects in its nest.

clue.text: Antacid tablets order by Connery — it's the wine

indicators.note: Sean Connery's famous slurred s means asking for something in his voice changes how it is heard

parts.note: Rennies are a British brand of antacid tablet, and Connery's lisp turns their s into sh

explanation.surface: A James Bond actor asks for indigestion pills to go with his wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Rennies are a UK indigestion remedy. Say the brand with Sean Connery's trademark 'sh' for 's' and you get the old name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish is an old term for wine from the Rhine region, as in hock, used by Shakespeare among others.

clue.text: Group recording Ms Lauper with support from Ms Blanchett?

indicators.note: a recording is something heard rather than read, so the names count for their sound

parts.words: Ms Lauper with support from Ms Blanchett
parts.note: singer Cyndi Lauper followed by actress Cate Blanchett

explanation.surface: Pop singer Cyndi Lauper cuts a track backed by actress Cate Blanchett.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group of people or firms combining for a shared business purpose.

clue.text: See 1
Difficult to get hold of ordinary loo rolls during the pandemic!

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so one word clasps the other

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A wry recollection of the empty shop shelves when everyone panic-bought toilet paper in 2020.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: loo rolls were scarce because shoppers stockpiled them, so the second half doubles as a picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet paper stockpiled at home in the Covid panic was the classic example of a secret store of supplies.

clue.text: Networked with mafioso regularly — didn't tell the truth about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the verb for lying goes round the 'it'

parts.note: to lie is not to tell the truth

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the gangster word is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of mafioso

explanation.surface: Someone who mixed with a gangster now and then lied about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to the letters just taken from mafioso, which sit inside LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to make contacts and cooperate, which is what networking means as a verb.

clue.text: Herb cookie filled with ganache longing to be eaten!

indicators.note: a filled biscuit has something inside it, so the cookie wraps what follows

parts.note: Oreo is a brand of sandwich cookie

indicators.note: something eaten disappears, so the yearning word vanishes from the chocolate one

parts.note: taken as written
to ache for is to long for

explanation.surface: A greedy cry about a chocolate-filled biscuit that someone is desperate to devour.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganache, a chocolate cream filling, fits the cookie picture, but here it only donates its first three letters once the longing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the mint family, widely used in Mediterranean cooking.

clue.text: Blubber lines seal, having an innate tendency to be clumsy

definitions.text: an innate tendency to be clumsy

indicators.note: having means containing, so the run of words holds the answer within them

parts.note: drop the first letter of blubber and keep the first of seal

explanation.surface: A seal's layers of fat seem to make it naturally ungainly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the second letter of Blubber to the first letter of seal. A lubber is a big clumsy oaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubberliness is the quality of being lubberly, that is awkward and loutish like a clumsy lout or landlubber.

clue.text: Dirty old man's brother starts to annoy nurse

parts.note: your father's brother is your uncle; old man is slang for father

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each is kept

parts.note: first letters of annoy and nurse

explanation.surface: A lecherous elderly man's sibling begins to irritate a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty old man' is a ready-made phrase that pulls Dirty into the wordplay, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means soiled or impure, a straightforward synonym for dirty.

clue.text: Lay a carpet, English, upper-class, the last from Axminster

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet
E is the abbreviation for English
U means upper-class in British usage

indicators.note: the last from a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: final letter of Axminster

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting a posh English rug, Axminster being a famous carpet maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Lay looks like a verb about fitting a carpet, but it is the adjective meaning non-professional. Axminster is a Devon town famous for carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay as an adjective means not belonging to a profession, so a lay person is an amateur.

clue.text: Gabriel fired shot — they fired back

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Gabriel opened fire and was met with return fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired back' sounds like returning fire, but it means they did their firing back in history: the Rifle Brigade was a British regiment, merged in 1966.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rifle Brigade was a former British Army regiment of riflemen, so its soldiers shot in years gone by.

clue.text: Oscar crashing doctor's Beetle

indicators.note: crashing a party means getting inside uninvited, so the letter goes in

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar has smashed into the doctor's VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Beetle look like the car, but it is just the insect; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dor is a kind of dung beetle, a crossword-friendly name for the insect that drones in flight.

clue.text: British rein in unruly Neapolitan master

indicators.note: unruly means out of control, so the letters break out of their order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
these six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Briton is told to control a disorderly person from Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini, born in Naples in 1598, was the great master sculptor and architect of Baroque Rome.

clue.text: To do with women nicking vehicle from capital outside station

indicators.note: outside means on the outer side, so what is left goes round the station
nicking means stealing, so the vehicle is taken away from the city's name

parts.note: Cardiff is the capital of Wales
a car is a vehicle
Sta is the abbreviation for station

explanation.surface: A crime report: a car is stolen from outside a station in the capital, involving women.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital here is the Welsh capital; once the vehicle is stolen from it, what is left goes round the station.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff was the staff for spinning, women's work, so the distaff side of a family is the female line.

clue.text: Broadcast unfortunate gag

indicators.note: broadcast words go out over the air and are heard, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a wretch is an unfortunate person

explanation.surface: A comedian's tasteless joke goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Unfortunate is used as a noun here, an unlucky person. Gag looks like a joke but is the verb for heaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to choke or heave as if about to vomit, which is exactly to retch.

clue.text: See Mordor easily on the way back circling airfield

indicators.note: travelling on the way back means going in the opposite direction, so read right to left
circling means going round, so the run of clue words surrounds the answer

parts.note: from the second E of See to the A of easily

explanation.surface: A Tolkien traveller spots Mordor without trouble while heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: Mordor is Sauron's dark land in The Lord of the Rings.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is a small airfield, the older word for a place where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Went back to be in Paris, having graded accommodation

indicators.note: accommodation is lodging, so one part is given room inside the other

parts.note: rated means graded
être is French for to be

explanation.surface: Someone returned to live in Paris, in a hotel with a star rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' asks for the French. Went back sounds like a return trip but means withdrew.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw or move backwards, so retreated is went back.

clue.text: Reckless — independent elected politician, ill-mannered, heartless fool

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
a Member of Parliament is elected
rude means ill-mannered

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle goes, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: nit is a fool; drop its middle letter

explanation.surface: A scathing verdict on a rude independent MP.
explanation.walkthrough: Nit is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means lacking care for consequences, a close synonym of reckless.

clue.text: Artist, constant member of The Mamas and the Papas, rounded figure

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant

parts.words: member of The Mamas and the Papas
parts.note: Mama Cass Elliot sang with the group
O is a round figure, the numeral zero

explanation.surface: An artist portrays a steady, full-figured singer from the 1960s group.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounded figure suggests Cass Elliot's build, but it is the round digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter and sculptor who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: High time for investors to flip about Turkey?

indicators.note: about means around, so the verb surrounds the country code

parts.note: to upend is to flip over
TR is the international code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Investors wonder if Turkey's economy is ripe for a turnaround.
explanation.walkthrough: High time reads as 'about time', but here it is a period when prices are high and climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: An uptrend is a sustained rise in market prices, a good period for investors.

clue.text: Mr T going missing — tightwad!

indicators.note: something going missing disappears, so that letter drops out of the title

parts.note: Mr written out in full
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mr T of The A-Team vanishes and someone grumbles about a stingy person.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr T looks like the actor, but expand Mr to MISTER and drop its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad is slang for a stingy person who hoards money, which is a miser.

clue.text: More muscular appearance initially feeds one's strength

indicators.note: something fed is put into a mouth, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: métier is the thing one is best at, one's forte

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of appearance

explanation.surface: Looking beefier at first feeds a person's physical power.
explanation.walkthrough: Strength means a strong point here, not muscle power.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaty describes a heavily built, brawny body, so meatier is more muscular.

clue.text: Cops, reportedly, turn Asian currency over

definitions.note: the definition is copse, signalled by its sound

parts.note: spin means turn

indicators.note: turned over means upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: Police apparently flip some Japanese money.
explanation.walkthrough: Cops is not the police: say it and you hear copse, a small wood. YEN reads upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a British word for a small wood or thicket, the same thing as a copse.

clue.text: Turns on former partner with cocaine, sex and tablets

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
C is slang for cocaine
it is a euphemism for sex
E is an ecstasy tablet, so Es are tablets

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid tale of a night with an ex involving drugs and sex.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for an ecstasy pill; 'it' for sex comes from phrases like 'doing it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone on is to arouse them, which is what excites means.

clue.text: Protested against factory material

definitions.meaning: first meaning: staged a sit-in at a workplace, written as two words
second meaning: a smooth glossy fabric

explanation.surface: Workers protested against the factory's choice of material.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers in a sit-in occupy their factory, so they sat in; joined up, the two words make the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, lustrous fabric, so it is a material; sat in describes occupying a factory as protest.

clue.text: Bringing joy, say, embracing classical language

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece wraps its arms around the other

parts.note: eg means for example, or say
Latin is the classical language of Rome

explanation.surface: Learning a classical language is a source of delight, as a classicist might say.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to make very happy, so elating is filling with joy.

clue.text: Driver's club lying around golf range

indicators.note: lying around something means being placed on either side of it

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer's driver is left on a driving range.
explanation.walkthrough: Driver, club, golf and range all point to golf, but range is the cooker. An Aga is a large heat-storage cooking range found in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga is a brand of heavy cast-iron kitchen stove, and a range is that kind of cooker.

clue.text: Questionable American Pastor infiltrating religious group

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside a group secretly, so these letters are placed within

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
US for American
P is an abbreviation for pastor

explanation.surface: A dubious American preacher has wormed his way into a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspect as an adjective means open to doubt, so questionable.

clue.text: Joined wife at home, beset by recurrent depression

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the earlier pieces sit inside
recurrent means running back, so the hollow word is read backwards

parts.note: a dent is a depression in a surface
in means at home
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man married a woman who stays home but keeps suffering bouts of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression seems to be the mood, but it is a hollow in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinned means paired or linked together, as towns are twinned, so joined.

clue.text: Drunken orderly entertaining northern lecturer in the city

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so the attendant word holds the others
drunken means staggering about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A tipsy hospital orderly is hosting an academic from the north in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Orderly looks like an adjective meaning tidy, the opposite of drunken, but it is the hospital attendant whose letters get mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Londonderry, also called Derry, is a city in Northern Ireland.
